subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should timestamped config backups preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points, or may the migration intentionally prune them on first write?
rationale: Config backups may be the user's only rollback path, and repository policy treats config recovery and migration behavior as compatibility-sensitive, so automation should not decide the permanent upgrade contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve Legacy Recovery Points
options.body: Require this PR or a replacement to retain existing `.bak.N` files until they are safely migrated into the timestamped retention set with owner-only permissions.

options.title: Accept Pruning On Upgrade
options.body: Allow first-run cleanup to delete numbered backups, but document that product decision and require explicit upgrade proof showing the remaining recovery behavior.

options.title: Keep Numbered Ring For Now
options.body: Close or defer the timestamp suffix direction and keep the shipped numbered ring as the stable backup contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve Legacy Recovery Points
recommendation.body: Require this PR or a replacement to retain existing `.bak.N` files until they are safely migrated into the timestamped retention set with owner-only permissions.
